title: Oatcakes with green beans and ricotta

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, flour, butter, ricotta, green beans and lemon are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, a board, a baking tray and a saucepan, and pressing out oatcakes is within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: The oat, flour, butter and water ratio makes a pressable dough, 20 minutes at 180°C fan crisps thin oatcakes, and 12 oatcakes with 250g each of beans and ricotta is a fair snack for four.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes covers mixing, pressing, cutting, trimming and chopping, and the 20-minute bake matches the cook time, with the 4-minute bean boil fitting inside it.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including salt, lemon and chives, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted except water is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: A generous 250g of just-cooked green beans in a lemony dressing is the substance of the topping, which suits a light late-July snack.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Wholegrain oatcakes with ricotta and plenty of green beans make a filling snack of real food.
